purpose: Use Tag for a read-only category or outcome word on an item (Production, Beta, Allowed) that is not a lifecycle state. The state of a resource is a StatusIndicator, a number is a Badge, a removable or selectable token is a Chip, and a level on the critical → info scale is a SeverityTag. A compact, read-only word on an item, colored by `severity` so the category or outcome reads at a glance (Production in primary, Blocked in danger). It takes an optional leading icon, a pill shape with `rounded`, and two sizes; it is never interactive and never counts.
useWhen: Label or categorize an item with a short descriptive text, optionally with a leading icon or pill shape.
Show a status/category with severity color via `severity`.

Mark the one value a list highlights (the Owner role in a users table) with `severity="highlight"`: the brand orange as a tint, orange text on `--primary-mask`, like the success, info and warning tints.
avoidWhen: It is purely a count or one-glance status label → use `badge`.
The user can select or remove it (filters, multi-select values) → use `chip`.
related: badge` — denser count/short-label indicator with no icon affordance.
bestPractices: Severity comes from `severity`; the optional icon is decorative — keep it `aria-hidden`.

Pick the severity by meaning: `success` Active, `warning` Pending, `neutral` Inactive or a neutral category (Developer, Viewer), `info` a second role (Admin), `highlight` the one value to single out (Owner), `primary` a solid brand label. Do not use `danger` for a state that is only off (Inactive): it reads as an error.
Do not restyle a Tag with colour classes to get a tint; every tint is a `severity`.
Use `rounded` for the pill shape rather than a custom radius.
